survey: A gold three-arm candelabra seen from the front, with the camera a little above it. A round, domed base sits on the ground. Its rim is a fairly open ellipse, which shows the top of the base from above. A turned central stem rises straight up from the base, with a knop in the middle and a collar where the arms join. Two U-shaped arms leave that collar, curve down and up again, and lie in the same front-facing plane, so their bends match. Each arm ends in a cup with a drip pan, and the stem ends in a third cup. The drip pans are ellipses seen from above, and they are a bit narrower than the base ellipse because they sit higher and closer to eye level, which is correct. Three upright cream candles sit in the cups. Their sides are vertical and parallel to the stem, and their tops are only slightly visible, which fits a viewpoint just above them. The flames point straight up. The base meets the ground evenly, at the angle its ellipse implies. Every part reads as one camera view.
